resources.string: Hear calls and talk with your iPhone’s own microphone and speaker. Android keeps call audio away from apps, so Pairline starts a small helper through Wireless debugging, a switch in Developer options that you turn on. No extra app and no root. Both phones also need to be on the same Wi-Fi.
This phone runs Android %1$s. Call audio on the iPhone needs Android 10 or later. Calls still ring on the iPhone, and you talk on this phone.
Connect this phone to Wi-Fi. Then in Developer options, turn on Wireless debugging and tap Allow. Pairline can’t turn it on for you; that’s up to you.

Tap Pair. In Wireless debugging, tap “Pair device with pairing code”. Pairline’s notification pops up: tap “Enter code” and type the 6 digits shown on screen. If you miss it, swipe down from the top and open Pairline’s notification. You do this only once.
Now tap “Pair device with pairing code” in Wireless debugging.
Tap “Enter code” in Pairline’s notification and type the 6 digits. Swipe down from the top if you don’t see it.
That code didn’t work. Type the code that’s on screen now; it changes each time the pairing screen opens.
Pairing didn’t finish. Keep “Pair device with pairing code” open and try again.
Paired. Android lists Pairline under Wireless debugging › Paired devices.
Allow Pairline’s notifications first: the pairing code is typed into one.
Happens by itself after the steps above.
Starts when Talk on iPhone is on.
Running. It keeps running until the phone restarts.
Pairline couldn’t find Wireless debugging. Check that it’s on and this phone is on Wi-Fi, then try again.
The helper didn’t start. Try again. If it keeps failing, turn Wireless debugging off and on.
Settings → About phone → Software information: tap “Build number” 7 times, then enter your PIN. Developer options appear at the bottom of Settings.
Settings → About phone: tap “OS version” (HyperOS or MIUI version) 7 times. Developer options are under Settings → Additional settings.
Settings → About device → Version: tap “Build number” 7 times. Developer options are under Settings → Additional settings.
Settings → About phone → Software version: tap it 7 times. Developer options are under Settings → System management.
Settings → About phone: tap “Build number” 7 times, then enter your PIN. Developer options are under Settings → System.
In Developer options, turn on USB debugging. Connect this phone to a computer that has Android’s adb tool and tap Allow on the phone.
Once after every restart of this phone. Pairline’s helper then keeps running until the next restart.
Without Wi-Fi, or if pairing doesn’t work: turn on USB debugging, connect a computer with adb and run this command once after each restart.

When you answer on the iPhone, the call’s audio moves to the iPhone. Also turns on the keypad, mute and speaker from the iPhone.
Pairline learns what works on this phone from your answers after calls. This forgets them.
Android turns Wireless debugging off when the phone restarts. Turn it on again and Pairline starts its helper by itself. Pairline reminds you with a notification.
Some banking apps won’t open while Wireless debugging is on. Once Pairline’s helper runs, you can turn Wireless debugging off again: calls keep playing on the iPhone until the phone restarts.
Stops the helper and deletes Pairline’s key. Also remove “Pairline” under Wireless debugging › Paired devices.
Call audio goes over your Wi-Fi, encrypted end to end. It’s never recorded or stored.
In Wireless debugging, tap “Pair device with pairing code”. Then type the 6-digit code here.

Keep the pairing screen open for a moment.
Check the 6-digit code on screen and try again. It changes each time the pairing screen opens.
Keep “Pair device with pairing code” open and type the code again.
Pairline is starting its helper. Calls you answer on the iPhone can now play there.
The phone restarted, so call audio is back on this phone. Tap and turn on Wireless debugging: Pairline then starts its helper by itself. Calls still ring on the iPhone meanwhile.
The phone restarted, so call audio is back on this phone. Run the command from Talk on iPhone on your computer once. Calls still ring on the iPhone meanwhile.
What does Wireless debugging do here? Does it need root?

Android lets only its own debugging tool reach call audio. With Wireless debugging on, Pairline starts a small helper with that tool’s rights, from its own app: no extra app and no root. The helper only carries call audio and handles the call keypad, mute and speaker. It stops when the phone restarts, and “Forget pairing” removes Pairline’s access for good.
Why does call audio go back to this phone after a restart?

Android turns Wireless debugging off every time the phone restarts, and the helper stops with it. Pairline then shows a notification: tap it and turn Wireless debugging on, and Pairline starts its helper by itself. Until then calls still ring and work on the iPhone, with the audio on this phone.
An app complains that debugging is on

Some banking and payment apps refuse to open while Developer options or Wireless debugging are on. Pairline never turns them on by itself. Once Pairline’s helper is running you can turn Wireless debugging off; calls keep playing on the iPhone until the next restart.
I hear calls on the iPhone, but they can’t hear me

Some phones don’t let any app feed audio into a call. Then you hear calls on the iPhone and talk on this phone. After each call the iPhone asks how it sounded; your answers help Pairline try another way on the next call.
Optional: hear and answer calls on the iPhone itself. Set up once with Wireless debugging; no extra app.
Turns on during your next call.
